about: Registry of every figure, diagram, table, screenshot and audio example the horde 1.0 user manual needs (B451). One entry per [[FIG:id]] / [[TAB:id]] / [[AUD:id]] placeholder in docs/manual/NN-*.md; tools/manual_scaffold_check.py keeps the two in step. Field meanings and statuses: docs/manual/README.md.

entries.purpose: Show the reader what horde looks like before anything else.
entries.content: The full horde 1.0 window on its default page with the init patch loaded, at default size.

entries.purpose: One picture of the whole instrument.
entries.content: Block diagram: OSC 1 and OSC 2 (SCALPEL on the swarm), Sub, noise -> filters -> mixer/routing -> FX rack -> master limiter -> out; modulation, morph and the intent bus drawn as layers acting on all blocks.
entries.source: docs/H2-PLAN.md parts table; ADR-190 roster

entries.purpose: Let the reader hear the swarm's coupling as its signature.

entries.purpose: Let the reader hear the fixed four intents.

entries.purpose: Point the reader at the right chapter for a task.

entries.purpose: Show that the engine is two SCALPEL oscillators.
entries.content: OSC 1 and OSC 2 side by side, each a swarm of members carrying blade 1 and blade 2, both feeding the mixer; what they share (voice, pitch, envelopes) drawn between them.
entries.source: B327 lineup; docs/design/scalpel-horde-engine.js (the composed engine golden)

entries.purpose: Show the path one note takes inside a voice.
entries.content: Note -> voice (amp envelope, blade envelopes, glide) -> N members (base wave + blade 1 + blade 2 + edge correction - DC) -> pan -> sum x amp env x velocity -> decimation when oversampled -> output saturation. Drawn without formulas.
entries.source: specs/SPEC-SCALPEL.md §2 signal flow; docs/design/scalpel-horde-engine.js

entries.purpose: Show how members are spread in pitch.
entries.content: A pitch axis with N = 3, 5 and 9 members placed evenly across ±detune cents around the played note.
entries.source: specs/SPEC-SCALPEL.md §3 member frequencies

entries.purpose: Let the reader hear what more members do.
entries.content: Three 3 s renders of the same note and detune with N = 1, 3 and 9; no FX; peak-normalised alike.
entries.source: Deterministic render of the C++ engine, one note, members N = 1, 3, 9 at fixed detune

entries.purpose: Show what coupling does to the members' phases.
entries.content: Members as dots on a phase circle at K = 0 (scattered, drifting), K = +1 (locked cluster) and K = -1 (evenly splayed), with the order parameter R drawn as an arrow.
entries.source: specs/SPEC-SCALPEL.md §3 coupling; reference/kuramoto-views.html

entries.purpose: Let the reader hear coupling as one continuous control.
entries.content: 12 s render of a held note while K sweeps from -1 through 0 to +1; fixed detune and N; no FX.
entries.source: Deterministic render of the C++ engine: K swept -1 -> 0 -> +1

entries.purpose: Contrast a settled note start with a free one.
entries.content: Two short phrases, the same notes, settled start then free start.
entries.source: Deterministic render once the onset controls are audited

entries.purpose: Name the parts of a blade.

entries.content: Rows Sync, FM reset, FM free, Noise, Fold, Ring, Crush: what happens inside the blade, the character, a typical use, which controls matter most.
entries.source: specs/SPEC-SCALPEL.md §4.2 modes, subject to the B376 keep/cull decisions

entries.purpose: Show each mode's effect on one cycle.
entries.content: Seven small waveform plots, one per mode, same base wave, position, width and cut rate.
entries.source: Rendered single cycles from the C++ engine (or the composed JS until the port)

entries.purpose: Let the reader hear each blade mode.
entries.content: Seven 3 s renders, same phrase and settings, mode changed each time, announced in order.
